headline: HSIE Results Daily: Divi’s Laboratories, Tata Steel

highlights: HSIE Research is also available on Bloomberg ERH HDF <GO> & Thomson Reuters 09 November 2026 HSIE Results Daily HSIE Results Daily Contents Results Reviews ■ Divi’s Laboratories: EBITDA (+76% YoY) beat ours/consensus estimates, as strong sales growth of 35% YoY (CS grew 54% YoY, generic API +12% and nutraceutical +13%) and higher gross margin (+739 bps YoY) of 67.9% were partly offset by higher costs.
Divi’s reiterates its expectation of double-digit revenue growth and sustaining higher EBITDA margin in FY27.

Peptides to stay as a strategic area of investment; customer programs progressing across multiple stages of development; qualification and validation activities for several peptide fragments are expected to advance over the coming quarters, alongside capacity expansion in both solid-phase and liquid-phase peptide synthesis by adding a few more 3KL SPPS capacities.

It continues to see pricing pressure in the generic API business, which it expects will be offset by volume growth; it expects to sustain base business growth and incremental growth from new launches.
valuation: Peptides to stay as a strategic area of investment; customer programs progressing across multiple stages of development; qualification and validation activities for several peptide fragments are expected to advance over the coming quarters, alongside capacity expansion in both solid-phase and liquid-phase peptide synthesis by adding a few more 3KL SPPS capacities.

We expect strong sales growth visibility (23% CAGR over FY26–29E), with improved profitability (EBITDA/PAT CAGR ~30/29%), supported by multiple growth levers like GLP-1 supply opportunity, scale-up in contrast media, ramp-up at the Kakinada plant, commercialization of capex plans, gradual pick-up in generic API, and steady nutraceutical business.
Factoring in the strong beat in Q2, we have raised EBITDA by ~24/10% for FY27/28E and revised the TP to INR 11,470, based on 43x Q2FY29 EV/EBITDA (implying 63x PE).
watch: Tata spent INR 33/69bn in capex in Q2/H12FY27 on the ongoing expansion, which led to net debt increase of ~INR 70/113bn in Q2/H1FY27 to INR 921bn (as of Sep’26). ▪ Con call KTAs and outlook: Tata guided for higher volume offtake in H2FY27 compared to H1.
